Get the edge list with uncertainty

Source: R/bison_model.R
get_edgelist.Rd

Returns the estimated edge weight of every dyad as a data frame: the posterior median and a credible interval, which contains the true value with the given probability according to the model. Use it to report or export edge weights, or to work with them in other software.

Usage

get_edgelist(obj, ci = 0.9, transform = TRUE)

Arguments

obj

A fitted bison_model object.

ci

Width of the credible interval, e.g. 0.9 for a 90% interval.

transform

If TRUE (the default), edge weights are on the natural scale (probabilities for binary models, rates for count models). If FALSE, they're on the link scale used inside the model (log-odds for binary models, log rates for count models). In models with an intercept or other effects, the natural-scale values are for an observation where those effects are 0.

Value

A data frame with one row per dyad and columns node_1, node_2, median, and the lower and upper bounds of the credible interval (named after their quantiles, e.g. 5% and 95%). Values are rounded to three decimal places.

See also

draw_edgelist_samples() for individual posterior draws of the edge list, summary.bison_model(), plot_network().

Examples

sim_data <- simulate_bison_model("binary", aggregated = TRUE)
fit_edge <- bison_model(
  (event | effort) ~ dyad(node_1_id, node_2_id),
  data = sim_data$df_sim,
  model_type = "binary_conjugate",
  priors = get_default_priors("binary_conjugate")
)
head(get_edgelist(fit_edge))
#>   node_1 node_2 median    5%   95%
#> 1      1      2  0.711 0.216 0.975
#> 2      1      3  0.498 0.194 0.802
#> 3      1      4  0.383 0.100 0.754
#> 4      1      5  0.733 0.422 0.935
#> 5      1      6  0.684 0.350 0.929
#> 6      1      7  0.585 0.274 0.853
